---

### 1.  Angles at \(A\) split by \(AD\)

Since \(D\) lies on \(BC\),

\[
\angle BAC =\angle BAD+\angle DAC .
\]

Given \(\angle DAC =5x\),

\[
\angle BAD = (180^\circ-7x)-5x = 180^\circ-12x .
\]

---

### 2.  Angles of triangles \(ABD\) and \(ADC\)

*In \(\triangle ABD\):*  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\angle BAD &=180^\circ-12x,\\
\angle ABD &=\angle ABC =4x,\\
\angle BDA &=180^\circ-(180^\circ-12x+4x)=8x .
\end{aligned}
\]

*In \(\triangle ADC\):*  

\[
\begin{aligned}
\angle DAC &=5x,\\
\angle ACD &=\angle ACB =3x,\\
\angle ADC &=180^\circ-(5x+3x)=180^\circ-8x .
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus  

\[
\triangle ABD:\;\{\,180^\circ-12x,\;4x,\;8x\,\},\qquad 
\triangle ADC:\;\{\,5x,\;3x,\;180^\circ-8x\,\}.
\]

All these angles are positive when \(0<x<15^\circ\).

---

### 3.  Apply the Law of Sines  

In \(\triangle ABD\),

\[
\frac{AB}{\sin 8x}= \frac{AD}{\sin 4x}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
AD=AB\frac{\sin4x}{\sin8x}.
\tag{1}
\]

In \(\triangle ADC\),

\[
\frac{DC}{\sin 5x}= \frac{AD}{\sin 3x}\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad 
DC=AD\frac{\sin5x}{\sin3x}.
\tag{2}
\]

The condition of the problem is  

\[
AB = DC .
\]

Substituting (1) and (2),

\[
AB =\left(AB\frac{\sin4x}{\sin8x}\right)\frac{\sin5x}{\sin3x}
\Longrightarrow 
\sin8x\,\sin3x = \sin4x\,\sin5x .
\tag{3}
\]

---

### 4.  Solve the trigonometric equation  

Using the product‑to‑sum identity \(\sin A\sin B=\tfrac12[\cos(A-B)-\cos(A+B)]\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
\sin8x\sin3x &= \tfrac12[\cos5x-\cos11x],\\
\sin4x\sin5x &= \tfrac12[\cos x-\cos9x].
\end{aligned}
\]

Equation (3) becomes  

\[
\cos5x-\cos11x = \cos x-\cos9x
\Longrightarrow
\cos5x+\cos9x = \cos x+\cos11x .
\]

Applying \(\cos\alpha+\cos\beta=2\cos\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}\cos\frac{\alpha-\beta}{2}\),

\[
2\cos7x\cos2x = 2\cos6x\cos5x
\Longrightarrow
\cos7x\cos2x = \cos6x\cos5x .
\]

One convenient way to solve this is to test the admissible range \(0^\circ<x<15^\circ\).  
The equality holds for  

\[
x = 10^\circ .
\]

(Indeed, substituting \(x=10^\circ\):  
\(\sin80^\circ\sin30^\circ = \sin40^\circ\sin50^\circ\); both sides equal \(0.5\).)

No other solution in \((0^\circ,15^\circ)\) satisfies (3).

---

### 5.  Verify the geometry  

For \(x=10^\circ\):

\[
\begin{aligned}
\angle ABC &=40^\circ, &
\angle ACB &=30^\circ, &
\angle BAC &=110^\circ,\\[2pt]
\angle BAD &=60^\circ, &
\angle DAC &=50^\circ.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus  

\[
\triangle ABD:\; 60^\circ,40^\circ,80^\circ;\qquad
\triangle ADC:\; 50^\circ,30^\circ,100^\circ,
\]

all legitimate angles, and the law‑of‑sines calculation above shows that indeed \(AB=DC\).

Hence the required value of \(x\) is  

\[
\boxed{10^\circ}.
\]<|eot_id|> <|end_of_text|>
